title: Dominating Set by width of a supplied vertex order
task: Does G have a set of at most k vertices such that every vertex either belongs to the set or has a neighbor in the set?
encoding: A finite, simple, undirected, unweighted graph G and a nonnegative integer k.
parameter: The maximum cut rank over prefixes of the supplied vertex order, denoted by p. Cut rank is computed over the binary field.
coverage: Historical ETH and independently reviewed recoveries.

inputConditions.condition: The graph is monopolar, meaning that its vertices can be partitioned into an independent set and an induced disjoint union of cliques.

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm decides Dominating Set within the stated running time.

reader.title: Effective quadratic-width bound on monopolar graphs under FPT ≠ W[1]
historicalNote: Liu and Meng state the quadratic lower bound under ETH in Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.10. The FPT ≠ W[1] exclusion is a direct consequence of their construction and the source-size calculation in the linked derivation.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: Both bounds concern the same width interface and monopolar graphs. The W[1] recovery retains the quadratic scale with computable exponent and convergence. The explicit order and rank decomposition have polynomial length in graph order.
